page: Microsoft Azure E64s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and cryptography acceleration via VAES and SHA-NI.

The server is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include any bundled local storage, but it is Premium Storage capable, allowing external storage attachments. There are zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core CPU performance, with a Passmark CPU score of 80,219.92 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 63,502.15. Memory read bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 4,689.08 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 329.32 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database operations are a key strength, demonstrated by a Passmark database score of 29,091.56 and Redis SET throughput of 105.13 million operations per second. Single-core performance and small-model LLM inference speeds fall within average ranges. This hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale database hosting, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.

Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the server delivers strong multi-core performance and memory bandwidth, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU score of 80,219.92 and uncached read speeds of 329.32 GB/sec. It also demonstrates exceptional database efficiency, achieving 105.13 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-core speeds and LLM inference performance remain average, the instance's massive L3 cache and advanced instruction sets like AMX and AVX-512 make it highly effective for memory-intensive enterprise databases, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
